title: Conversational grounding: paper + blog digest (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick personal digest of a small reading list about conversational grounding (retrieval+tool grounding, multi-turn context grounding), plus practical takeaways we can test on Redwood. Not a polished literature review — working notes + concrete eval/experiment ideas for the next sprint.

Papers/blogs skimmed (short notes):
- "Grounding LLMs with retrieval: Survey and practical recipes" (blog, May 2030) — emphasizes mismatch between retriever training and downstream conversational behavior. Key point: retriever precision at top-1 matters more for short prompts than recall for long-context summarization.
- "Chain-of-thought + grounding" (arXiv, 2029) — shows that inserting retrieved snippets as discrete steps in CoT can reduce hallucination if retrieval is cited and the model is penalized for contradictions. Takeaway: structured insertion (labelled chunks) beats raw concatenation when the model is instructed to treat retrieved text as evidence.
- "Dynamic context stitching for multi-turn QA" (ICLR 2030 talk + slides) — describes chunk scoring + alignment with turn-level intents; uses reranker + alignment head to avoid stale context.

High-level thematic takeaways:
- Retrieval quality and alignment with expected turn intent is the real bottleneck for grounding in chat settings. A retriever optimized for static queries underestimates the need to prefer freshness and conversational salience.
- How we add evidence matters: tagged snippets + provenance metadata reduce hallucination compared to unlabelled concatenation.
- Latency and token cost tradeoffs: rerankers help avoid sending many long chunks into the model (saves IO/token), but introduce extra latency; batching and async reranking (speculative answers) are possible mitigations.

Concrete experiments to run on Redwood (priority order):
1) Small AB test: naive concat vs labelled-snippet insert (label=\"SOURCE: ...\") using same retriever. Metric: hallucination rate on a curated set (see dataset below), relevance precision@1, latency (p50/p95), token cost.
2) Retriever objective ablation: train/evaluate a reranker tuned for conversational salience (turn-aware features) vs vanilla BM25/embedding. Evaluate on multi-turn dataset: turn intent match, P@1, end-to-end final answer correctness.
3) Speculative reranking pipeline: fire model on top-1 local cache + async rerank secondaries; measure cases where speculative answer suffices vs when fallback improves correctness. Track additional cost and rollback frequency.
4) Quantization interaction: run the same pipelines on int8-quantized model variant to measure hallucination/fluency regressions when evidence is concatenated vs when model uses explicit citations.

Datasets / probe sets I want to assemble quickly:
- 200 multi-turn threads (internal support logs anonymized) where critical answer requires recent doc retrieval. Label ground-truth spans where answer can be found.
- 150 synthetic turn-by-turn queries derived from long docs (create a \"progressive reveal\" style dataset where the answer becomes obvious only after a specific turn).
- Small adversarial set (50 items) where distractor snippets are topically similar but contradictory in facts.

Metrics and instrumentation (must be product-actionable):
- Hallucination rate (binary human label per response) + short reason tag (missing-evidence, contradicted-by-evidence, inference-only).
- Evidence precision@k (do we include the correct span among top-k retrieved?).
- End-user correctness (binary) and helpfulness score (1-5).
- Latency: end-to-end p50/p95; split by retriever, reranker, generation.
- Token cost breakdown per route (retrieval payload vs model tokens).
- Failure-mode tracing: sample traces where model ignored retrieved evidence or invented facts despite evidence present.

Deployment/serving notes for Redwood:
- Annotate retrieved chunks with short provenance tokens: source_id, chunk_start, chunk_end, freshness_ts. Provide a minimal provenance header we can render in UI or pass to evaler.
- Rollout plan: Canary on 10% traffic with heavy telemetry (human review); watch hallucination rate and latency delta. If hallucination goes down and latency within SLA, expand.
- Autoscaling: reranker stage may need CPU burst capacity; ensure we have fallback route that uses only retriever if reranker quota exceeded.

Prompt formatting heuristics (practical knobs):
- Use explicit instruction: "Use only the text under SOURCES. If you cannot find an answer, say 'I don't know' and provide suggestions to find out."
- Insert retrieved chunks as: 
  [SOURCES]
  - SOURCE 1 (doc:ID:ts): <snippet trimmed to 200 tokens>
  - SOURCE 2: ...
  [/SOURCES]
  Then: \"Answer concisely and cite which SOURCE number you used.\"
- Token budget: prefer top-3 snippets capped at 600 tokens total; otherwise fallback to summary-of-summaries (reranker summary).

Open questions / unknowns (for discussion):
- How to define conversation-aware retriever scoring cheaply — features we can compute in real-time vs expensive fine-tuning? (suggested: recency, explicit mention overlap with last N turns, dialog act heuristic).
- How often does quantization amplify hallucination when retrieved evidence is present? Need small matrix of model-size x quantization-level x pipeline-type.
- Can we amortize reranker cost across similar queries in short windows? E.g., cache reranker scores keyed by canonicalized last-turn fingerprint.

Short-term TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- Pull 200 anonymized support threads, redact PII, and write short-turn extracts (action: Cleo + SRE for redaction).
- Implement labelled-snippet insertion in the infil pipeline (prototype in local harness; action: Mika).
- Add instrumentation hooks to record per-stage latencies and token counts (action: Hannah).
- Design small human eval rubric for hallucination annotations (binary + reason tags).

Notes-to-self / rough heuristics I kept coming back to:
- If retriever precision@1 > 0.6, simple concat often OK; if < 0.4, need reranker + stricter prompts.
- When evidence length gets long (>1500 tokens), chunk summaries or a reranker that returns condensed passages are more predictable and cheaper.
- Always include an explicit "I don't know" fallback in the prompt to reduce confident hallucinations — empirically reduces bad answers in pilot runs.

References I found helpful (to cite later):
- blog: "Practical grounding for chatapps" (May 2030) — pragmatic recipes and prompt patterns.
- arXiv: dynamic context stitching (ICLR slides)
- internal repo: grounding-probes (synthetic adversarial set, WIP)

End of scratchpad. Will refine into a proper experiment brief after the data pull + quick prototype.

Unresolved: pick a short name for the pilot (\"grounded-chat-canary\"?) and whether to run as hosted-api-only or dedicate a small dedicated node pool (dedicated helps isolate cost for reranker experiments).
